subject.title: Heartbeat skipped reason 'target-none' is misleading when delivery is disabled by default

question: Should OpenClaw preserve `reason: "target-none"` as the machine-readable heartbeat skip reason and add a disabled-delivery hint/display field, or rename the reason itself?
rationale: The value is exposed through Gateway/CLI output and asserted in tests, so the clearer rename and the compatibility-safe additive hint are both plausible but encode different product/API-contract choices.

options.title: Add an additive hint
options.body: Keep `reason: "target-none"`, add a disabled-delivery hint or equivalent display field, and update the CLI/status formatting plus regression tests.

options.title: Rename the reason
options.body: Change the machine-readable reason to a clearer value such as `delivery-disabled`, accepting the compatibility risk for users or scripts parsing the old value.

options.title: Leave current output
options.body: Keep `target-none` unchanged and rely on docs, accepting the existing operator confusion as low-priority UX friction.

recommendation.title: Add an additive hint
recommendation.body: Keep `reason: "target-none"`, add a disabled-delivery hint or equivalent display field, and update the CLI/status formatting plus regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the default-none heartbeat behavior and have the strongest history on the heartbeat delivery/status boundary.
